claims.text: The as-cast MgAlCuZnGd alloy has a non-equilibrium microstructure.
Mg and the other alloying elements are homogeneously distributed in the as-cast alloy.
Isothermal annealing at 300–500 °C for 1–10 hours promotes localized Mg segregation at grain boundaries.
Localized Mg segregation leads to incipient formation of a nanoscale Mg-rich oxide or amorphous passivating phase.
Mg diffuses to and segregates at grain boundaries during annealing.
Preferential oxidation of Mg-enriched regions produces a continuous protective passivating oxide network.
The passivating oxide network reduces active metal dissolution in corrosive environments.
The passivating oxide network slows oxygen ingress during high-temperature exposure.
Annealed specimens will have lower corrosion rates than as-cast specimens.
Annealed specimens will have greater high-temperature oxidation resistance than as-cast specimens.
Annealing in the specified range avoids excessive intermetallic coarsening.
The alloy maintains a density below 6 g/cm3.
The proposed controlled comparison is between as-cast specimens and specimens annealed in an inert atmosphere.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis permits either a Mg-rich oxide or an amorphous passivating phase, but the falsification rule requires formation of a Mg-rich oxide; formation of only the stated amorphous alternative could therefore satisfy the hypothesis while being classified as falsification.
